title: Eval quality drift for major customer due to stop-token normalization and sampling inheritance
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Quantiva Health (enterprise, private deployment + dedicated pools) reported sudden eval score degradation in their nightly regression suite after runtime-1.22 rolled out. Symptoms: model outputs sometimes omitted expected end-of-response markers or appended extraneous trailing text, causing automated evals to fail JSON parsing and lowering BLEU/EM scores. Behavior inconsistent across deployment modes: private and dedicated showed highest regressions, hosted customers showing smaller but measurable delta. Initial hypothesis pointed at sampling default change, but logs suggest combined interaction with gateway-level stop-token normalization and KV-cache reuse across multiplexed streams.
reproduction_steps: Use Quantiva's eval prompt set (linked in Confluence) against model-variant: redwood/gpt-large-std@v5 on a dedicated pool with runtime-1.22
Run with customer runtime config (no explicit sampling overrides) via private control plane and capture outputs and token-level traces
Compare outputs against pre-1.22 baseline using our eval harness (eval-run id: eval-20260228-quantiva)
Enable KV cache instrumentation (trace ids) and replay sequences with identical prompt prefixes to observe trailing-token carryover
Repeat test on hosted endpoint using same model + API flags to observe difference
root_cause_summary: A multi-factor regression: (1) runtime-1.22 introduced a change to sampling defaults for backcompat edge cases (implicit sampling inheritance when request field omitted) which caused some requests to switch from deterministic/top-k behavior to stochastic sampling; (2) the gateway normalization layer canonicalized stop sequences (trim + casefold + whitespace collapse) before tokenization, producing a different byte-to-token mapping for certain multibyte stop markers used by the customer; (3) an unrelated KV-cache reuse optimization in the serving runtime allowed cached key-value segments to bleed across multiplexed requests when stop-token alignment differed, producing trailing tokens in a subset of high-concurrency scenarios. The combination produced inconsistent stopping behavior and stochastic output variance that broke Quantiva's strict eval comparators.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix 1: Revert sampling inheritance change in runtime-1.22 gateway that allowed implicit sampling mode switches (rolled to canary on 2026-03-05)
Hotfix 2: Stop-token canonicalization moved from gateway pre-normalization to model-proximal canonicalizer to preserve original byte-patterns (PR #4892)
Hotfix 3: KV-cache guard: isolate per-request cache keys for multiplexed streams when stop-token canonicalization differs (PR #4896)
Added end-to-end regression tests in eval-harness that include customers' stop sequences and multibyte markers
Deployed immediate canary to Quantiva Dedicated pool, then gradual rollout to other dedicated/private pools after 48h of stability metrics
